original_question: Let G be an infinite finitely presented group such that every subgroup of infinite index is free. Must G be isomorphic to either a free group or a surface group?
target_in_paper: Problem 21.138 in the 'New Problems (21st issue, 2026)' section of The Kourovka Notebook.
correct_elements: Your draft matches the paper's problem essentially verbatim: it asks about an infinite finitely presented group G such that every subgroup of infinite index is free, and asks whether G must be isomorphic to either a free group or a surface group. It also correctly avoids adding extra hypotheses such as one-relator, residual finiteness, hyperbolicity, or finite-index subgroup conditions, none of which appear in Problem 21.138.
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, the term 'surface group' should be spelled out, since the notebook problem states it without a local definition; the natural clarification is that this means the fundamental group of a closed connected surface.
If maximal explicitness is desired, one can state that the hypothesis ranges over all subgroups of infinite index, not only finitely generated ones.
refined_question: Let G be an infinite finitely presented group such that every subgroup of G of infinite index is a free group. Must G be isomorphic to either a free group or to the fundamental group of a closed connected surface?
justification: The draft is already extremely close to the paper's actual statement. In the current version of arXiv:1401.0300, the exact matching item is Wilton's Problem 21.138, which asks precisely this question and does not impose any further structural hypotheses. Because the notebook gives the problem as a standalone open question rather than as part of a theorem-proposition-conjecture chain, there is no nearer official reformulation to substitute, and the only worthwhile refinement is to make the phrase 'surface group' explicit so the question is self-contained.
